chronicle.text: Heibeim found that what Kaivail had told them was wrong, and trusted them less for it.
Roukarail tied fiber and fiber together with fiber and was left with something to carry things in: the first carrier.
Teihei came back for food left 5 weeks before, and it was still there.
Thaiba tied wood and wood together with fiber and was left with something that floats and carries someone across water: the first raft.
Heibeim gathered food that had grown where seeds had been dropped: the first harvest from seed left in the ground.
Shokoum drank from the sea and it did not quench their thirst.
Shokoum tied a bundle they had tied and stone together with fiber and was left with something heavy on a handle: the first club.
Lesaikul went back to a thing they had made a third time, to see it happen again: the first deliberate testing.
Teihei told Lesaikul that Keihagail could be believed: reputation passed on by word.
Heidas scratched a mark </\o> into rock.
Teidouk buried seed on purpose, having seen it come back as food: the beginning of farming.
Thaiba crossed open water on something that floats and came ashore on land nobody could walk to from where they set out.
Teihei struck flint with flint and stared at what happened.
Teihei struck flint with flint and was left with a sharp edge: the first blade.
Kaivail attacked Heibeim: the first violence.
At (34, 37) the heap of things people had left grew big enough to keep out a fifth of the winter cold: the first dwelling. Lesaikul had put in the most.
Lesaikul struck flint where dry things lay, and they caught: the first fire made by people.
Nekok survived an attack by a bear.
Teihei crossed open water on something that floats and came ashore on land nobody could walk to from where they set out.
Heibeim crossed open water on something that floats and came ashore on land nobody could walk to from where they set out.
Nougek set food aside on purpose, having found it there when it was needed before: the beginning of keeping stores.
Shailou took up striking flint with stone from a mark: the first thing learned from a record.
Shailou came on the mark <o|\> and took it to mean flint being struck: the first mark read as a message.
Houshevuk tied a blade and wood together with fiber and was left with a sharp point on a long shaft: the first spear.
Shailou tied a club and fiber together with fiber and was left with something warm to wear: the first wrap.
Higol found that what the mark <\|^> seemed to say was wrong, and put less faith in that mark.
4 people now take the mark <v//> to go with stone being struck, and have for two years. Nobody decided this; it grew from where the mark was made and seen.
3 people now tell that wolves mauled Nekok. It was a bear. The story changed as it was passed on.
